```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2,
  out.width = "100%"
)
```

This vignette shows how to **export structured results** from
**`interact`** for quality control, reporting, or downstream tables.
The idea matches **“calculate once, use many times”**: fit the model,
then take all display numbers from **`tidy()`** (and comparison helpers),
not from re-typing forest-plot labels.

Getting started with **`cams()`**:
[`vignette("cams")`](cams.html).

## Setup and fits

We use the **`steroids`** IV/NIV example (same data path as
[`vignette("cams")`](cams.html)). **CAMS** uses **`method = "REML"`**
here; sensitivity analyses add **DA**, **AD**, and **SWADA**.

```{r setup, cache = TRUE}
library(interact)
library(dplyr)

steroids_obs <- steroids |> filter(n > 0)
steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events,
  bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events,
  di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = steroids_obs
)
des <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "NIV")

fit_cam <- cams(des, reference = "NIV", method = "REML")
fit_da <- da(des, reference = "NIV", method = "REML")
fit_ad <- ad(des, reference = "NIV", method = "REML")
fit_sw <- swada(des, reference = "NIV", method = "REML")
```

## Canonical export: `tidy(fit)`

**`tidy(fit)`** binds interaction, modifier, combined, and (optionally)
heterogeneity rows in one tibble. You can still call **`tidy(interactions(...))`**
when you need a single estimand. Typical columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **`estimate`**, **`std.error`**, **`conf.low`**, **`conf.high`** | Point and interval on the requested scale |
| **`type`** | e.g. **`Overall`**, **`Prediction`** |
| **`subgroup`** / **`level`** | Modifier label ( **`modifiers()`** ) |
| **`interaction`** | Contrast label ( **`interactions()`** ) |
| **`parameter`**, **`label`** | Heterogeneity summaries ( **`heterogeneity()`** ) |

```{r export-estimands}
results <- tidy(
  fit_cam,
  estimands = c("interaction", "modifiers", "combined", "heterogeneity"),
  type = "Overall",
  exponentiate = TRUE
)
knitr::kable(
  results |>
    filter(estimand != "heterogeneity", type == "Overall") |>
    select(estimand, level, interaction, type, estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
  digits = 2
)
```

Add run metadata once (reference, inference, reporting IF) for audit
trails:

```{r metadata}
meta <- tibble::tibble(
  package = "interact",
  method = "CAMS",
  inference = "REML",
  reference = "NIV",
  scale = "OR",
  reporting_if = as.numeric(ifrac(fit_cam, ifrac = "interaction"))
)
knitr::kable(meta, digits = 3)
```

## Pre-specified sensitivity analyses

**`sensitivity()`** fits **DA**, **AD**, **SWADA**, and **CAMS** on the same
data; **`compare()`** aligns them on one table—useful as **sensitivity** rows
in a report (not as a single “consensus” estimate).

```{r compare-interactions}
sens <- sensitivity(des, reference = "NIV", method = "REML", silent = 2)
cmp_ix <- compare(
  sens,
  estimand = "interaction",
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  type = "Overall"
)
knitr::kable(cmp_ix, digits = 2, caption = "Interaction OR: construction sensitivity")
```

```{r compare-modifiers}
cmp_sg <- compare(
  sens,
  estimand = "modifiers",
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  type = "Overall"
)
knitr::kable(cmp_sg, digits = 2, caption = "Modifier ORs: DA vs SWADA vs CAMS")
```

**Note.** Under default weights, **SWADA** matches **AD** for the
interaction; both appear in the interaction sensitivity table because they
answer different construction definitions.

## QC: one row lookup vs the printed summary

QC should recover the same **Overall** interaction as **`print()`** /
**`interactions()`**:

```{r qc}
from_tidy <- cmp_ix |>
  filter(approach == "CAMS") |>
  pull(estimate)
from_api <- tidy(
  fit_cam,
  estimands = "interaction",
  type = "Overall"
)$estimate
stopifnot(
  length(from_tidy) == 1L,
  length(from_api) == 1L,
  isTRUE(all.equal(from_tidy, from_api, tolerance = 1e-6))
)
```

## Handoff to layout tools

**`interact`** does not render regulatory TLGs. After **`tidy()`**, use
your table package of choice (**`gt`**, **`gtsummary`**, **`flextable`**, …)
on the tibble. Keep **computation** (this export) separate from
**layout**, in line with CDISC **Analysis Results Data** thinking: structured
statistics first, formatted output second.

Minimal **gt** example (skip if **`gt`** is not installed):

```{r gt, eval=requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)}
results |>
  filter(estimand != "heterogeneity", type == "Overall") |>
  select(estimand, level, estimate, conf.low, conf.high) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high), decimals = 2)
```

## Forest plots and exported numbers

Pooled **Overall** diamonds on **`forestplot(fit_cam)`** match
**`modifiers()`** / **`combined()`** at the reporting IF shown under the
axis. When QC fails, check **`exponentiate`**, **`type`**, and
**`reference`** match between the plot and **`tidy()`** calls.

```{r forest-qc, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, cache = TRUE}
forestplot(
  fit_cam,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  favours = c("Lower mortality", "Higher mortality")
)
```
